why: Deleting the head is a special case unless a dummy node sits in front of it. With a dummy, every deletion is the same move: from the predecessor, skip the next node. It teaches the dummy head for deletions.
hints: To delete a node from a singly linked list, which node's pointer do you change?
Its predecessor's next. The head has no predecessor, which is why it is awkward; give it one with a dummy node.
prev = dummy (dummy.next = head). While prev.next exists: if its value matches, prev.next = prev.next.next; otherwise advance prev. Return dummy.next. O(n).
pitfalls: Do not advance prev right after deleting: the new prev.next may also need deleting ("7,7,7").
Every node may be removed; the answer is then an empty list (dummy.next is None).
